title: Pivot article engagement by subscription tier
prompt: You maintain a news app that logs daily article engagement metrics. The `daily_engagement` table stores one row per (date, subscription_tier, metric) combination, with columns `engagement_date`, `subscription_tier` (one of: 'free', 'basic', 'premium'), `metric_type` (one of: 'articles_opened', 'articles_completed', 'conversions'), and `metric_value` (integer count for that day/tier/metric). Write a query that pivots this data into a wide-format report showing, for each engagement_date, the SUM of metric_value across all tiers for each of the three metric types. The output columns must be: `engagement_date`, `articles_opened`, `articles_completed`, `conversions`. If no rows exist for a given metric_type on a date, show 0 instead of NULL. Order the result by `engagement_date` ascending. Edge case: some dates may lack rows for certain metric types; some dates may have multiple rows (different tiers) for the same metric type.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE daily_engagement (engagement_date DATE NOT NULL, subscription_tier VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, metric_type VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, metric_value INT NOT NULL);
example_input_data: INSERT INTO daily_engagement (engagement_date, subscription_tier, metric_type, metric_value) VALUES ('2024-01-15', 'free', 'articles_opened', 120), ('2024-01-15', 'basic', 'articles_opened', 80), ('2024-01-15', 'premium', 'articles_opened', 45), ('2024-01-15', 'free', 'articles_completed', 30), ('2024-01-15', 'premium', 'articles_completed', 20), ('2024-01-15', 'basic', 'conversions', 5), ('2024-01-16', 'free', 'articles_opened', 95), ('2024-01-16', 'premium', 'articles_completed', 18);
test_data: INSERT INTO daily_engagement (engagement_date, subscription_tier, metric_type, metric_value) VALUES ('2024-02-01', 'free', 'articles_opened', 150), ('2024-02-01', 'basic', 'articles_opened', 110), ('2024-02-01', 'premium', 'articles_opened', 60), ('2024-02-01', 'free', 'articles_completed', 40), ('2024-02-01', 'basic', 'articles_completed', 35), ('2024-02-01', 'premium', 'articles_completed', 28), ('2024-02-01', 'free', 'conversions', 3), ('2024-02-01', 'basic', 'conversions', 7), ('2024-02-01', 'premium', 'conversions', 12), ('2024-02-02', 'free', 'articles_opened', 88), ('2024-02-02', 'premium', 'articles_opened', 52), ('2024-02-02', 'free', 'articles_completed', 22), ('2024-02-02', 'premium', 'conversions', 9), ('2024-02-03', 'basic', 'articles_opened', 72), ('2024-02-03', 'basic', 'articles_opened', 15), ('2024-02-03', 'free', 'articles_completed', 19), ('2024-02-03', 'basic', 'articles_completed', 14), ('2024-02-03', 'premium', 'articles_completed', 11), ('2024-02-04', 'free', 'conversions', 2), ('2024-02-04', 'basic', 'conversions', 4), ('2024-02-05', 'premium', 'articles_opened', 38), ('2024-02-05', 'free', 'articles_opened', 102), ('2024-02-05', 'basic', 'articles_opened', 67), ('2024-02-05', 'premium', 'articles_completed', 16), ('2024-02-06', 'free', 'articles_opened', 91), ('2024-02-06', 'basic', 'articles_completed', 27), ('2024-02-06', 'premium', 'conversions', 8), ('2024-02-07', 'basic', 'articles_opened', 55), ('2024-02-07', 'premium', 'articles_opened', 42), ('2024-02-07', 'free', 'articles_completed', 25);

composite_moves: pivot: GROUP BY engagement_date with SUM(CASE WHEN metric_type = 'X' THEN metric_value END) per target column, COALESCE to 0

hints: Think about how to turn each metric_type value into its own column while summing across all tiers for that metric on each date.
Use CASE expressions inside SUM to isolate rows for each metric_type, then group by engagement_date. Wrap each SUM with COALESCE to turn NULLs into 0.

The pattern is: SELECT engagement_date, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN metric_type = 'articles_opened' THEN metric_value END), 0) AS articles_opened, ... FROM daily_engagement GROUP BY engagement_date ORDER BY engagement_date.
answer_key:
SELECT
  engagement_date,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN metric_type = 'articles_opened' THEN metric_value END), 0) AS articles_opened,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN metric_type = 'articles_completed' THEN metric_value END), 0) AS articles_completed,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN metric_type = 'conversions' THEN metric_value END), 0) AS conversions
FROM daily_engagement
GROUP BY engagement_date
ORDER BY engagement_date;

_meta.scenario: a news app tracking article completion and subscription conversion
